build.note: Read from the saved raw capture with the L3207 cell reader and the EBX decoder; no export, no new capture.

question: Does the L3323 damage rule reproduce EA's 1.3.1.0 figures for the launchers, C-4, the SLAM, the jet bombs and the IFV HEI-T round?

sourceFacts.method: For each weapon the projectile's direct damage and the explosion's blast damage were taken (registry default where a row exists, otherwise the asset's own value, recorded separately), with the material ID stored on each object. Field_674633de was read for each material against targets 119, 121 and 120 in both level grids and combined by the L3323 rule, then compared with every figure EA states for that item in the 1.3.1.0 notes. The notes were fetched on 9 October 2026 and saved as text in the run folder.

control.description: Seven items reproduce all of EA's figures (26 numbers); the RPG control of L3323 (grid 2 / 9 / 10 for material 125) was re-read in the same run.

rawCheckSummary.tool: scripts/frosty-raw-check.py --manifest (stored values: raw-checks.json; grid reads: all-grid-rawchecks.json)

slam.numericFit: 199 to 363 would follow from a direct product of 131.25 plus the body blast 100 (ceil(0.75 x 131.25) + 100 = 199, 2 x 131.25 + 100 = 362.5). The stored product is 130 x 0.4375 = 56.875. No stored damage value gives 131.25; 300 x 0.4375 equals it, but the stored 300 is the EFP's initial speed, so that is a coincidence of numbers, not a source.

c4RegistryRow.note: A registry row under owner PB_C4 stores BlastDamage 180. No saved file is named PB_C4; the saved C-4 projectile file is PNS_C4, whose own BlastDamage is 100. 100 x 3.5 gives EA's 350; 180 x 3.5 would give 630. No stored link between the row and PNS_C4 was found, and the pair is not in the disputed-property list.

inference: The L3323 rule holds for the M136 AT, MBT-LAW, SLM-93A, IGLA, C-4 and both jet bombs. Against tanks the blast part is added without the hit-quality factor, which is why blast-only weapons have a single tank figure.

EA's 1.3.1.0 notes state the hit-quality steps themselves (turret 75%, body at least 100%, side 150%, rear 200%). The rule's 0.75 to 2 is taken to be these steps; which stored field carries them is still not traced (L3325).
PB_Bomb_GBU39 BlastDamage follows the registry default 240 and not the asset's 200, provided EA's Mk82 line describes this file.
The two bomb lines match with the names crossed. Whether EA's notes or the file names are the wrong way round is not decided here.
For launchers and C-4 without a registry damage row the asset's own value is the live value. The unlinked registry row PB_C4 BlastDamage 180 does not give EA's figure.
unresolved: Bomb identity. Test: one bomb from the fighter jet on a full-health tank's body; about 320 (GBU-39 file) or about 435 (Mk82 file).
C-4. Test: one pack on a full-health tank; 350 (asset 100) or 630 (registry row 180).
IFV HEI-T low figure, EA 10 against the rule's 12. Test: one HEI-T hit on a tank's turret.
M4A1 SLAM, EA 199 to 363 against the stored 143 to 213.75. Test: SLAM against a tank's side, front and underside.
EA's figures are from update 1.3.1.0. Test: one M136 AT hit on a tank's rear (550) and one MBT-LAW hit (240) on the current build.
siteImpact: None. No Analyzer data, simulation or UI change.

leads.title: The damage rule extended to launchers, C-4 and jet bombs
leads.summary: The L3323 rule reproduces all of EA's 1.3.1.0 figures (26 numbers) for the M136 AT, MBT-LAW, SLM-93A, IGLA, C-4 and both jet bombs; the bomb lines match with the names crossed. PB_Bomb_GBU39 BlastDamage follows the registry (26 of 73 disputed properties). The IFV HEI-T low figure (EA 10, rule 12) and the SLAM (EA 199 to 363, stored 143 to 214) do not fit. 13108 raw reads matched.
leads.reopenWhen: An in-game reading for a jet bomb, C-4, the HEI-T round or the SLAM, or a stored link that names which jet carries which bomb file.
leads.statusNote: 26 official numbers reproduced; bomb names crossed; HEI-T low figure and SLAM not reproduced; joins by name.
